dimensions.note: No settings, vault references or secrets in the models. gh and git use the environment's own auth (gh signed in, git credentials); nothing reads Deno.env or a token. The tracked vaults/local_encryption YAML holds only config (auto_generate), no key. CI passes SWAMP_API_KEY/SWAMP_SIGNIN_TOKEN only to the reusable publish job, with contents: read.

merged_cleanup logs on entry (method and PRs asked), one line per PR and the summary; each added git/github method logs before acting and when done. All use {placeholder} props, no interpolation. Nothing sensitive is logged; PR titles appear only for merged PRs.

Input (prNumbers, BranchName, 40-hex expect, owner/name repo) and a non-GitHub origin throw before any call or writeResource. Inside clean each runModel failure or throw becomes that step's failed/skipped status with git's message (by design: the spec wants per-step results), and the result is still written. Lease refusal (stale info) and non-fast-forward are distinguished from network/other failures (failed, not skipped). is_ancestor separates unknown-commit from other errors. gh errors carry exit code and stderr.

make test: 84 passed, 0 failed; deno check, fmt --check and lint clean. Tests run on real temp git repos with a bare origin and cover every AC1-AC9 path plus failures (network pull, thrown call, unmerged -d refusal, unknown head, bad input, non-GitHub origin) and a no-force assertion over all calls. Hand-written contexts rather than createModelTestContext. Caveat: the @swamp/git built-ins (status, remove_worktree, branch, pull, is_ancestor, config) are fakes in fixture_test.ts whose parity with @swamp/git 2026.10.23.1 is asserted in the README and a manual real run, not by a test.

Worktree, local branch and origin branch already gone are reported as already done (cleanup_delete_branch probes with rev-parse, cleanup_delete_remote_branch with ls-remote, remove_worktree's alreadyAbsent); a clean that stopped part-way is finished by running clean again (tested). Every write step is re-checked first (worktree head/branch/lock/clean; origin via the lease), so interruption leaves only safe partial states.

No HTTP; GitHub is read through gh. gh pr view/list JSON is validated with zod (state enum, headRefOid, headRefName, mergedAt datetime) and malformed rows are dropped or raise a named error. gh pr list is capped at 30 by latest activity and reports truncated=true when gh returned the cap; sorted by mergedAt afterwards.

Deno.Command(...).output() with stdin null collects and closes all pipes on every path; no files or temp dirs are created by the models. Tests dispose their temp repos with await using. No cloud resources created.

Checked README, LICENSE (additionalFiles), workflows and test fixtures, and the rest of the repo for public visibility. Fixtures use github.com/acme/widgets and test@example.com. Workflow recipe tags and CLAUDE.md carry the Capture request URL on loopback 127.0.0.1:3002 (no real host, required by the recipe's source field). spec/ files name the outcome owner with email already redacted to redacted@example.com; .swamp.yaml repoId and the vault config are not secret. No real IPs, internal hostnames, account IDs or credentials found.

All schemas are plain z.object without passthrough; ItemSchema.strict() is asserted in a test against real check/clean items. Mechanical checks: every writeResource (result; cleanupWorktrees, cleanupBranchHeads, cleanupBranchDelete, cleanupRemoteBranchDelete; cleanupMergedPrs, cleanupPullRequest) writes exactly its schema's fields with real values; cleanup_merged_prs carries an honest truncated flag; headBranch and head are stripped from items.
result: lifetime infinite, garbageCollection 20 (history of runs). All added git/github resources: ephemeral, garbageCollection 10.

Not a CRUD lifecycle model: check/run are read-only reports and clean is a one-shot action over git/GitHub state; the added methods are single-purpose list/delete helpers. No create/update/sync lifecycle applies.

No swamp-level labelled checks are declared; the safety checks are deliberately inline and not skippable: inputs and a GitHub origin are validated before any call, and before each step clean re-reads the worktree (branch, head, lock, uncommitted changes) and the main checkout, and deletes origin's branch only under --force-with-lease on the PR head. Making these skippable would weaken the spec's no-orphan guarantee.

merged_cleanup writes spec result under distinct instances result (run), check and clean, same schema. Added methods write one instance per call (cleanup-worktrees, cleanup-branch-heads, cleanup-branch-<branch>, cleanup-remote-branch-<branch>, cleanup-merged-prs-<repo>, cleanup-pr-<repo>-<n>); no collision within one execution. Sanitising maps a/b and a-b to the same name across calls, which only versions over the earlier data.
No method reads back stored state; every read is live (git/gh via runModel results), as the re-check-before-each-step design requires. No dataRepository access.

First release: model version and manifest version are both 2026.11.11.1; the only earlier manifest version (2026.10.26.1) was the template placeholder and nothing in the repo shows a published earlier model schema, so no upgrades entry is needed.
